subject: Archaeology
title: Angkor Wat: Hidden in the Jungle
description: A micro-lesson that makes Angkor Wat: Hidden in the Jungle usable.

hook.text: A French explorer in 1860 stumbled onto the largest religious monument on earth, swallowed by Cambodian jungle.

buildup.text: Angkor Wat was built in the 12th century for the Khmer Empire. Its moat alone is three miles around.

discovery.text: LiDAR scans in 2012 revealed that Angkor was a sprawling metropolis of over a million people.

twist.text: The city collapsed partly because its massive water system could not survive prolonged drought.

climax.text: Angkor Wat never truly vanished — Buddhist monks maintained the central temple for centuries.

punchline.text: The 'lost' temple was never lost. Monks kept it alive while the city fell.

quiz.question: What did LiDAR scans reveal about Angkor in 2012?
options: The temple was much older than previously believed
Angkor was a sprawling metropolis of over a million people
A network of underground tunnels connected all the temples
